data.content_ref: inline:The proposed relation is 'inheritance,' but the target's own refutation clause exposes that the dependence is in the wrong direction for genuine inheritance. The isolated artifact is said to 'generalize' SRC_012's procedure into a protocol 'that applies to any Diophantine constraint system.' Under genuine inheritance, the child must preserve the parent's behavior on the parent's own inputs. The target admits the protocol is refuted if it fails on the canonical instance S=138, structure=three-consecutive-even — which is precisely SRC_012's domain. So the target is only safe if the generalization happens to reproduce the parent on one specific input, not because it inherits the parent's method. This is a coincidence-then-verification scheme, not an inheritance hierarchy: any sufficiently broad constructive protocol that 'proposes via structure, verifies via constraints' will contain SRC_012's single instance as a special case by accident, without any methodological lineage. The shared-label 'verification-first' is attached to two unrelated roles (SRC_012 does arithmetic reconstruction of a proposed triple; the artifact does generic constraint checking). The real relation is abstraction-with-lossy-specialization, not inheritance; the target overstates the relation's kind.
